docs.text:
Note 29-10-2026

日本語版: 新GT実験の概要

This page describes a new experiment to collect ground truth (GT) data: GPS tracks where the true place of each stop is known. It is for lab members who may take part.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text: In the first experiment, participants followed a planned scenario. This time there is no scenario. Participants use their own phones and spend their time freely in a new place. This gives data closer to real life.

docs.title: 2. At a glance
docs.text: Item Details Participants About 20 students Place [TBD] (staying at an Airbnb) Length 2-3 days (dates: [TBD]) GPS Own phone + Reem-san's app (app name: [TBD]) Reward [TBD]

docs.title: 3. What you do
docs.text:
• Spend the days as you like. There is no fixed route and no group rule. Going alone or with others is your choice.
  • Keep the app running for the whole period.
  • Tap a button when a stop starts and when it ends (see 5).
  • Each night, spend about 10 minutes checking the day's record (see 6).

docs.title: 4. What counts as a stop
docs.text:
You make a stop when you stay in one place for 5 minutes or more. Places you only walk past are not recorded. A stop has one of three types.

Type Examples Building Shops, restaurants, cafés, museums. Moving between floors of one building is still one stop. Street Waiting on a sidewalk, standing at a roadside stall. Open space Parks, plazas, riversides.

If you are not sure of the type (a covered shopping street, an underground mall, a café terrace, and so on), pick the closest type and say a few words about the place in a voice memo.

docs.title: 5. How to log
docs.text:
You log with [TBD: a button in the app, or a form]. Each person logs their own stops.

  • Tap "start" when a stop begins and "end" when it finishes. The time is saved automatically, so you never need to check a clock and write it down.
  • Choose the type (building / street / open space).
  • For the place name, a voice memo of about 3 seconds is enough (optional), for example "going into Lawson". Only your own voice is recorded, for a few seconds.
  • Photos keep the time they were taken, which helps when checking later (optional).
  • If you forget to tap, log the stop when you notice, or add it at the evening check.

docs.title: 6. Evening check
docs.text:
• It takes about 10 minutes. Look at the day's GPS track on a map (how: [TBD]).
  • Add any missing stops and fix any times that are off.
  • Do it the same day, while you still remember.

docs.title: 7. Phone checklist
docs.text:
Both iPhone and Android can stop apps that run in the background. Check these before the trip.

  • [ ] App installed and tested beforehand
  • [ ] Location set to "always allow", precise location on
  • [ ] Battery saver (battery optimisation) off for this app
  • [ ] Bring a power bank
  • [ ] Tell the organiser your phone model and OS version

docs.title: 8. Privacy
docs.text:
• You sign a consent form before taking part.
  • What is collected: GPS positions and times, your taps, voice memos and photos (optional), and your phone model.
  • The location of the Airbnb is hidden in the analysis.
  • You can pause recording at any time. Please tell the organiser when it was paused.
  • Who can see the data, and for how long it is kept: [TBD]

docs.title: 9. Timeline
docs.text:
1. Pilot: 2-3 people try the app and the logging for half a day ([TBD])
  2. Briefing: explain the steps to everyone and check phone settings together ([TBD])
  3. Trip: 2-3 days ([TBD])
  4. Every night: upload the data; the organiser checks that no app has stopped

docs.title: 新GT実験の概要
docs.text:
Note 29-10-2026

English version: New GT experiment

この資料は、新しい正解データ（GT: ground truth）を集める実験の概要です。GTとは、各ストップで「本当にどこにいたか」が分かっているGPSデータのことです。参加を考えている研究室のメンバー向けです。

docs.title: 1. 目的
docs.text: 前回の実験では、決められたシナリオに沿って動いてもらいました。今回はシナリオがありません。参加者は自分のスマートフォンを使い、新しい場所で、自由に過ごします。そのため、実際の生活に近いデータが集まります。

docs.title: 2. 概要
docs.text: 項目 内容 参加者 学生 約20名 場所 [TBD]（Airbnbに宿泊） 期間 2〜3日（日程: [TBD]） GPS 自分のスマホ + Reemさんのアプリ（アプリ名: [TBD]） 謝礼 [TBD]

docs.title: 3. 参加者がすること
docs.text:
• 好きなように過ごしてください。決まったルートやグループのルールはありません。一人でも、誰かと一緒でも自由です。
  • 期間中は、アプリをずっと動かしておきます。
  • ストップの始まりと終わりに、ボタンをタップします（5を参照）。
  • 毎晩10分ほど、その日の記録を見直します（6を参照）。

docs.title: 4. 「ストップ」とは
docs.text:
同じ場所に5分以上いたら、1つのストップです。歩いて通り過ぎただけの場所は記録しません。ストップには3つのタイプがあります。

タイプ 例 建物 店、レストラン、カフェ、美術館。同じ建物の中なら、階を移動しても1つのストップ。 道路 歩道で人を待つ、道ばたの屋台の前で立ち止まる。 屋外空間 公園、広場、川沿い。

どのタイプか迷ったとき（屋根のある商店街、地下街、店のテラス席など）は、近いタイプを選び、音声メモで状況を一言説明してください。

docs.title: 5. 記録の方法
docs.text:
記録には [TBD: アプリ内のボタン、またはフォーム] を使います。一人ひとりが自分のストップを記録します。

  • ストップが始まったら「開始」、終わったら「終了」をタップします。時刻は自動で記録されるので、時計を見て書く必要はありません。
  • タイプ（建物 / 道路 / 屋外空間）を選びます。
  • 場所の名前は、3秒ほどの音声メモで言うだけでOKです（任意）。例：「ローソンに入る」。録音するのは自分の声を数秒だけです。
  • 写真を撮ると撮影時刻が残るので、あとで確認するときに役立ちます（任意）。
  • タップを忘れたら、気づいたときに記録するか、夜の見直しで追加してください。

docs.title: 6. 毎晩の振り返り
docs.text:
• 約10分です。その日のGPSの軌跡を地図で見ます（見る方法: [TBD]）。
  • 抜けているストップを追加し、ずれている時刻を直します。
  • 記憶が新しいうちに、その日のうちに行ってください。

docs.title: 7. スマホの準備
docs.text:
iPhoneもAndroidも、裏で動いているアプリを止めることがあります。出発前に次を確認してください。

  • [ ] アプリをインストールし、事前に試した
  • [ ] 位置情報を「常に許可」、「正確な位置」をオン
  • [ ] このアプリの省電力（バッテリー最適化）をオフ
  • [ ] モバイルバッテリーを持っていく
  • [ ] スマホの機種とOSのバージョンを担当者に伝える

docs.title: 8. プライバシー

docs.title: Nested probabilities
docs.text:
Plan On-going Doctoral 26-10-2026

New work from the meeting on 20-10-2026 (Publications and doctoral plan). Builds on Assignment framework.

Goal: two levels of probability for each stay.

  1. Which type? How likely the person is in a building, on a street, or in an open space. The master's model gives this level.
  2. Which one? Which building, which street, which open space. This level is computed separately for each type, so within one type the probabilities add up to 100%.

Example: a stay has three candidate buildings, and level 1 gives building 70%. Level 2 then shares 100% among those three buildings.

This is the first extension named at the group meeting on 26-10-2026: identify which building, which street, or which open space.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
All three types are tried together first. If that is too hard, one type at a time, to see which works best.

  1. Labels for level 2. The ground truth (GT) only says the type of each stay, not the exact building, street or open space. A script suggests one entity for each physical stop (one place, recorded by up to five phones). For buildings it compares the place name in the survey form with the building names in the map. Otherwise it takes the entity closest to the stay. Each suggestion is then checked by hand on a map. One stop can have more than one correct entity, for example a mall made of several building outlines, or a street cut into several pieces.
  2. Level 2 from the current model. The master's model already gives every candidate a score. Inside one type, these scores already split 100% among that type's candidates, so level 2 needs no new model at first. The check: how often the true entity gets the highest share, and whether that beats simply taking the nearest entity.
  3. A new fit, only if step 2 is weak. Train the model on the exact entities as well, or use a nested logit (a model that first picks the type, then the entity inside it). The type accuracy (0.718) must not drop.

Part of Doctoral plan.

docs.title: Street segmentation
docs.text:
Plan On-hold Doctoral 16-10-2026

Supporting work for Sequence-aware assignment.

A flaw found in the master's thesis: how streets are cut into segments affects the assignment. See Limitations.

Goal: exploratory research to find the most robust way to segment streets for this kind of assignment work.

docs.title: What the street map is now
docs.text:
• Streets come from the MAPPLE pedestrian network: each link (a piece of path between two points of the network) is widened to its real width. There are 33,982 links. 68% of them are straight lines between two points, and only about 5% bend clearly.
  • The road surface for cars is not a street in this map. It is open space on purpose, because it is not a place for walking. This is the main reason the segmentation needs to be rethought.
  • Because of this, a person standing on a sidewalk is often recorded inside open space. For the stays labelled "Street", the GPS point closest to the stay's centre lies in open space 46% of the time, and inside a street piece only 28% of the time.
  • Open space is what is left after buildings and streets are removed. Rivers are not part of it.

docs.title: Direction score bug
docs.text:
The direction score (f_directional) in the thesis never used the real direction of a street: every street was treated as pointing east (found 19-10-2026). The fixed code takes each street's direction from its centerline. So the thesis results say nothing yet about whether shorter or longer street pieces help the direction score.

First result with the real direction (experimental rerun, 19-10-2026): the small movements inside a stay follow the street direction about as much as random movement would. People standing on a street even move slightly less along the street than people near it (0.61 against 0.63, where 0.64 means random). In the refitted models, the direction score gets a clear weight when all three types share one weight (+3.49, t = 6.8). With one weight per type, the street weight is negative (about -5), so movement along a street counts against that street. A raw signal close to random and a street weight that points the wrong way make the direction score weak evidence at the moment, whatever the segmentation.

Part of Doctoral plan.

docs.title: 2. Indoor and outdoor stays on a map
docs.text:
Four stays from the ground truth: two inside buildings, one on a street and one in an open space. The map is at the start of Section 4.2 (validation).

  • Black dots are the GPS points of the stay, joined in time order. The star is the medoid: the GPS point closest to the centre of the stay.
  • Nearest-entity rule. The usual deterministic method: the stay goes to the place nearest the medoid (or the place that contains it). The dashed outline shows that place.
  • Below each map: what the nearest-entity rule says, and the probability the framework gives each type (B building, S street, O open space). The probabilities are out of sample: the model that gives them was fitted without that stay (Grouped cross-validation).
  • What the maps show. Indoors (a, b), the points do not stay inside one building: they spread into the streets and open space around it (σ about 19 m). In (b) the medoid falls in open space. On the street (c), the medoid falls inside the building next to the sidewalk. In the park (d), most points are in open space, but the medoid falls on a park path that the map counts as a street segment (Street segmentation).
  • In all four, the framework gives the correct type the highest probability. The four stays were chosen among stays the framework gets right, so they show how the method works, not how often it works.

Over all 907 stays:

Accuracy Building Street Open space Nearest-entity rule 0.479 0.501 0.281 0.607 Framework (out of sample) 0.718 0.893 0.492 0.450

Where the two methods agree and disagree (number of stays, out of 907):

Rule correct Rule wrong Total Framework correct 351 (both right) 300 (only the framework) 651 Framework wrong 83 (only the rule) 173 (both wrong) 256 Total 434 473 907
  • The bold cells are where the two methods disagree. When they disagree, the framework is right more than three times as often (300 against 83).
  • In 9 stays the medoid lies inside a building and a street at the same time (the two map layers overlap). The rule then picks building.

docs.title: 3. One stay through every step
docs.text:
The street stay of map (c) goes through the method in Sections 3.1 to 3.3 (Framework overview). A participant stood on the sidewalk of Fukutomachi Road for 10 minutes. After downsampling, the stay has 10 GPS points, and they are very spread out (σ = 46.5 m).

Step 1: candidates (Candidate selection). Every place within 10 m of at least one GPS point: 5 buildings (B1 to B5), 5 street segments (S1 to S5) and 4 open spaces (O1 to O4). Only 1 of the 10 points falls inside a street. Three fall inside building B1, three inside a building further east, and three in open space about 50 m to the west.

Step 2: scores (the same table is in the paper, Section 3.2).

Candidate Distance to medoid (m) f_distribution f_distance f_temporal f_directional B1 0.0 0.55 1.00 0.93 0.07 B2 42.3 0.38 0.95 0.38 0.08 B3 3.8 0.27 1.00 0.27 0.08 B4 13.5 0.24 0.99 0.29 0.07 B5 32.4 0.16 0.97 0.16 0.08 S1 2.8 0.93 1.00 0.93 0.92 S2 32.3 0.29 0.97 0.29 0.93 S3 26.5 0.23 0.98 0.23 0.27 S4 27.2 0.23 0.98 0.23 0.27 S5 31.9 0.03 0.97 0.03 0.27 O1 1.8 0.93 1.00 0.93 0.07 O2 10.8 0.37 1.00 0.29 0.07 O3 28.4 0.27 0.98 0.27 0.07 O4 34.7 0.07 0.97 0.07 0.07

How to read it:

  • f_distribution: S1 (the sidewalk) and the open space O1 next to it are near the points for 93% of the time. Building B1, which contains the medoid, gets 55%.
  • f_distance: above 0.95 for every candidate. The points are so spread out that distance does not separate the candidates for this stay.
  • f_temporal: close to f_distribution for most candidates. This overlap is why the final model drops it.
  • f_directional: the steps between points follow the road. S1 and S2 (the two segments of Fukutomachi Road) score 0.92 to 0.93, the cross streets 0.27, every building and open space below 0.08.

Step 3: utility (a second table, Section 3.3). The final weights turn the scores into a value \(V_k\) for each candidate. Two more inputs enter. - share_type: 5 of the 14 candidates are streets, so every street loses 5.156 × 5/14 = 1.84. - sigma: the points are spread out, so every street and open-space candidate gains 1.045 × 1.332 = 1.39. S1 has the highest value, 1.89.

Step 4: probability.

Building Street Open space Final model (fitted on all 907 stays) 0.32 0.50 0.17 Out of sample (fitted without this stay) 0.35 0.45 0.20 Nearest-entity rule B1 (wrong)

The framework picks street, which is correct. It still gives almost a third to building, so the reader can see that this stay is uncertain.

docs.text:

The same sentence explains why the distance weights for street and open space are negative: at α = 2.979, f_distance is close to 1 for most candidates (median 0.96), so these weights act mostly as a fixed extra value for each type.
  • Definitions that were missing: the medoid, share_t (the share of the stay's candidates that have the candidate's type) and the σ input.
  • share_t wording. Section 4.2 now speaks of a share, not a count of competing segments, which matches share_type.

docs.title: Code check and adopted rerun
docs.text:
Thesis bug fixes and adopted rerun. A check of the code against the thesis on 19-10-2026 found six problems: two in the scores and four in the ground truth cleaning. The fixed pipeline (run C) is now the official one, and the thesis, paper, poster, abstract and slides use its numbers. The old versions are archived.

  • Accuracy on unseen data does not change significantly (0.716 → 0.718; McNemar p = 0.74 on the 895 shared stays).
  • Recall moves from open space (0.492 → 0.450) to street (0.427 → 0.492). Building barely moves (0.896 → 0.893).
  • The final model loses the f_distribution × share_type term (VIF 10.7, just above the limit of 10) and has 11 parameters instead of 12.
  • Most thesis decisions hold: 10 m search distance, no ASC, one shared direction weight, the simple model beats Random Forest and XGBoost, downsampling does no harm.

Points for sensei:

  1. α is bounded from below only. The fit is almost flat above 2.4, and the model uses the inside best point, 2.979.
  2. One test close to its limit decides the model shape: VIF 10.7 against 10. The other test, one shared direction weight against one per type, is clear (p = 0.115).
  3. The ASC raises accuracy on unseen data, so the case against it rests on its copy of the street direction score (r = 0.94) and the sign flip that follows (Model 5: alternative-specific constants (rejected)).
  4. Crowded street candidates explain the street errors. The open-space errors still have no cause.

docs.title: Doctoral direction
docs.text:
The end goal is Sequence-aware assignment: an assignment that knows which stays came before.

Milestones

  • Comprehensive literature review. Re-read the key papers the research is built on, some of them old, and search for newer work on the same ideas. On-holds
  • Transferability. Show that the framework works on other data. Sensei prefers another city before MILES. The open question is ground truth for that city; the most likely source is data from the University of Tokyo. On-holds

Supporting work

  • Street segmentation. Find the most robust way to cut streets into pieces. In the current map the road surface for cars counts as open space, so a person on a sidewalk often lands in open space: for street stays, the GPS point closest to the stay's centre lies in open space 46% of the time and in a street piece 28% of the time. With real street directions, movement inside a stay follows the street about as much as random movement would. On-holds
  • GPS toy data. A GPS generator with a known true place for every stay, so each source of error can be switched on alone. Two programs: one makes people and their activity chains, the other turns them into GPS points in the MILES format. The literature search (Consensus Report) supports the design. Its weakest part is the stay-level offset in the error model, so the offset stays a setting with a wide range. Rejected

docs.title: MNL model development
docs.text:
Progress Master 19-07-2026

The first time the model was fitted to the cleaned ground truth (907 stays with known answers). MNL is the type of model used here: it turns scores into probabilities (see Glossary).

  • Search distance. A search distance (R_buffer) of 10 m works better than 15 m for every model tried: R_buffer: 10 m vs 15 m.
  • Six models compared, each adding something to the one before: Model 1: base → Model 2: share-type and sigma → Directional scope ablation (3a vs 3b) → Model 4a: alternative-specific parameters → Model 5: alternative-specific constants (rejected) → Interaction term screen (α = 1). Accuracy (the share of stays with the correct type) rose from 0.540 to 0.733.
  • α. The setting α controls how fast the distance score drops with distance. It was tuned to 2.98 on Model 4a (Alpha calibration). With α at 2.98, the extra term f_distance² was no longer useful and was removed (The f_distance² artifact).
  • Best model at that time. Separate weights for each place type (Model 4a at the tuned α). 13 parameters, accuracy 0.733. The combined term f_distribution × share_type is significant on its own, but it overlaps too much with the other terms to keep (Stepwise VIF elimination).
  • High VIF values. Some important terms have high VIF values (a warning sign that terms overlap). Here that comes from how the model is built, and it is not a mistake: Multicollinearity is structural.

Later corrected by RQ1 rebuilt with grouped CV.

Linked from Assignment framework · Calibration · Thesis summary

docs.title: ML baseline
docs.text:
Progress Master 20-07-2026

Sensei's question: could machine-learning models such as Random Forest or XGBoost do much better? If yes, that would show how far the simple model is from the best possible result.

  • Result at the time. Random Forest did a little better (+2.0 percentage points in cross-validation, CV: testing on data the model did not learn from). XGBoost was about the same as the simple model. All tree models scored 100% on their own training data, which means they memorized it: ML baseline, stay level (superseded).
  • GPS spread. σ (how spread out the GPS points are) was one of the most important inputs for both tree models, even though it has only a small weight in the simple model: Sigma in tree importance.
  • Decision. The tree models were not adopted, because they cannot give a clear probability for each place.

This comparison was later replaced by a fairer one in RQ2 diagnostics and RQ3 ceiling check.

Linked from Complexity and transfer · RQ2 diagnostics and RQ3 ceiling check · Thesis summary

docs.title: RQ1 rebuilt with grouped CV
docs.text:
Progress Master 21-07-2026

All models were tested again with a fairer method.

  • The problem. Three phones recorded each stop at the same time. In the old cross-validation (CV), one phone's recording of a stop could be in the training data and another phone's recording of the same stop in the test data. That made results look better than they really are. All models were fitted again with Grouped cross-validation, which keeps all recordings of one stop together (Model progression).
  • What changed. The best model kept the same form and the same accuracy on its training data (0.727). On unseen data it scored 0.710 ± 0.030. This is the fairer number.
  • What stayed the same. Alpha calibration found α = 2.979 again. The model with ASC terms was rejected again (Model 5: alternative-specific constants (rejected)), and f_distance² was again shown to be a side effect of the wrong α (The f_distance² artifact). Removing weak terms (Stepwise VIF elimination) gave the 13-parameter model, the core of Model 4a.
  • Follow-up. f_directional does not need a separate weight for each place type (p = 0.115, not significant). The 11-parameter version with one shared weight does better on unseen data (0.718 ± 0.028) and is more stable: f_directional: shared vs split → Final model.

The 11-parameter model is the final model of the thesis (Section 5.1.8).

Linked from Assignment framework · Calibration · MNL model development · Thesis summary

docs.title: RQ2 diagnostics and RQ3 ceiling check
docs.text:
Progress Master 23-07-2026

Checks on the Final model. The model was not fitted again; these checks only look at its results.

  • RQ2, where the model fails. The model finds 89.3% of building stays, but only 49.2% of street stays and 45.0% of open-space stays. When it gets a street or open space wrong, it usually says "building" (Confusion matrix). The reason: street stays have the most street candidates around them, and the share_type term punishes that (Candidate density bias toward building). The difficult test sets are difficult for all three types (Fold difficulty).
  • RQ3, could another model do better? On unseen data, the simple model beats Random Forest and XGBoost (0.718 vs 0.705 and 0.697), even though both fit the training data better (ML ceiling check, row level). This reverses the result from ML baseline.
  • Appendices. The thesis appendices were put together from existing data: Final model correlation matrix, Self-report form, the five experiment groups, and Ground truth drop list. One count did not match, and the thesis has since been corrected: Ground truth cleaning.
  • Discussion draft. A four-part draft of the discussion, which became the Discussion section of the thesis: Problem and positioning and Error analysis.

docs.title: Does downsampling matter?
docs.text:
Progress Master 29-07-2026

Sensei's question. Before fitting, the survey data is downsampled: points are removed so that it looks like MILES. Does this step change the result? To check, the Final model was fitted again on the full survey data, without downsampling.

  • Downsampling does no harm. On unseen data, the downsampled data gives 0.718 ± 0.028 and the full data gives 0.709 ± 0.032. The model is more stable with downsampled data (condition number 1,869 vs 4,735) (Raw-density refit).
  • α changes. With the full data, the fit keeps improving up to the search limit, α = 6, instead of stopping at 2.979. But it changes very little over a wide range of α, so neither value is pinned down well (Raw-density alpha profile).
  • Side finding. Downsampling also makes the search area around each stay smaller, so each stay gets fewer candidates (Downsampling shrinks the candidate search area).

docs.text:
Thread Master 05-08-2026

Part of Thesis summary. Research question 2: where the final model makes mistakes, and why.

  • Confusion matrix: the model finds building stays about twice as often as street or open-space stays
  • Candidate density bias toward building: street stays have the most street candidates around them, and the model punishes that
  • Fold difficulty: street accuracy follows how hard each test set is; open space is low in every test set
  • Tension with the street-space argument: what this means for the idea that streets are real places of activity
  • Candidate density as boundary-matching difficulty: a similar problem known from GPS research on roads and sidewalks

docs.title: Thesis summary
docs.text:
Thread Master 05-08-2026

Beyond the Building: A Probabilistic Framework for GPS Assignment Under Positional Uncertainty

When a phone records GPS points while someone stays in one place, the points do not tell you exactly where the person was. In a city, the GPS error is often larger than the distance between a building, the street in front of it, and the open space next to it.

Most studies solve this by picking the nearest building. This thesis does something different. For each stay, it gives a probability for building, street and open space, so the uncertainty stays visible. The model learns how to do this from a field survey in Hiroshima, where participants recorded where they really were.

docs.title: Where it stands
docs.text:
• The final model has 11 parameters. On data it had not seen, it picks the correct type for 71.8% of stays (± 2.8%), written as grouped CV accuracy 0.718 ± 0.028 (Final model).
  • It finds 89.3% of building stays, but only 49.2% of street stays and 45.0% of open-space stays. When it gets streets or open spaces wrong, it usually says "building". For streets, the reason is how the street map is cut into pieces; for open space, the reason is still open (Confusion matrix, Candidate density bias toward building).
  • Random Forest and XGBoost fit the training data better, but on unseen data this simpler model does better (ML ceiling check, row level).
  • The thesis is complete. The questions that were still open in these notes are answered in the final text (Final model, Ground truth cleaning, Tension with the street-space argument).
